Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www.dilg.com.ph OILG OPINION NO. 27 JUN 2019 s. 20B MAYOR FELIX A. SY, M.D. Municipality of Manjuyod Province of Negros Oriental Dear Mayor Sy: This has reference to your letter dated 20 February 2019 requesting for this Department's legal opinion on whether or not job salaries may be included under essential operating expenses. Per your letter, the 2019 Municipal Budget has yet to be approved by the Sanggunian. As a consequence, your municipality is operating under a reenacted budget pursuant to Section 323 of Republic Act No. 7160 (RA 7160), otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991. Our view is in the affirmative provided that the salaries of those under job order engagements were authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year. We refer to the provision on reenacted local budgets. Section 323 of Republic Act No. 7160 (RA 7160), otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 states: "Section 323. Failure to Enact the Annual Appropriations. - In case the sanggunian concerned fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during such sessions. If the sanggunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) days from the beginning of the fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the propased appropriations is passed by the sarwunian concerned. However, only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. xxx" (Emphasis supplied). The law specifies the items in the appropriation that are deemed reenacted and, thus, may be disbursed. The last sentence is instructive. To reiterate, only the annual appropriations for salaries and wages of existing positions, Statutory and contractual obligations, and essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith.

Further, our view is that the same shall be deemed included as an item under Maintenance and Other Operating Expense in the reenacted budget and are covered for the ensuing year. It shall not be under the expenditure item of Personal Services (PS) considering that Job Order workers are not considered employees of the government and that PS expenditure refers to payment of salaries, wages, and other compensation of employees of the government. Moreover, MOOE refers to those for support to the operations of government.2 We previously opined that Job Orders, on the other hand, covers a piece of work or intermittent job of short duration not exceeding six months on a daily basis and are not considered government service but are in the nature of contracts which is under the supervision and regulation by the DBM and the COA pursuant to Section l, Rule XI of Civil Service Commission (CSC) Memorandum Circular No. 40, s. 1998, as amended, and CSC MC No. 01, s. 2007. Hence, the same may be covered under the reenacted budget provided said contractual obligation was authorized in the annual and supplemental budget for the preceding year.3 Notwithstanding, this is without prejudice to the contrary opinion of the Department of Budget and Management, if' any, considering that it has the mandate and technical expertise on the matter. Very truly yours, By the authority of the Secretary MARIVEL C.
